addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- handoff: End-of-session handoff. Reconcile the project's tracking file (mark done resolved, promote every leftover to a live item with value+trigger, log decisions/debt/lessons), verify green via the project's oracle command, confirm nothing lives only in chat or a disposable note, persist a disposable resume prompt (with a cold-start reload list of the links that mattered this session) into the tracking file, checkpoint-commit, then compact the note. Project-agnostic. Use when wrapping up, pausing, "prep handoff", "close the session", or "generate a resume prompt".
- linkedin-review: Multi-agent parallel review of a LinkedIn profile against benchmarks, via Playwright MCP browser navigation. Spawns N specialized personas (decideur-client, commercial-esn, personal-branding, concurrent-freelance, copywriter, ats-keywords, seo-linkedin) in parallel, each producing an independent critique. Returns a synthesized report with convergences, conflicts, prioritized actions. Use when the user asks to audit/review their LinkedIn profile.
- review-plan: Multi-agent parallel review of a plan, design doc, or architecture proposal. Spawns N expert personas (product, security, performance, seo, devex, cloud-architecture, finops, compliance, accessibility) in parallel, each producing an independent critique. Returns a synthesized report with convergences, conflicts, and decisions to make. Use when the user asks to review a plan, audit a design, get multiple perspectives on a doc, or run a "multi-agent review".
- rtk: RTK (Rust Token Killer) proxy meta-commands. Use when the user asks for RTK token-savings analytics, command history, missed-opportunity discovery, or wants to bypass the auto-rewrite hook (rtk proxy). The PreToolUse hook auto-rewrites Bash commands transparently - do not invoke this skill for normal commands.
- add-contact: Create one CRM Contact via add-contact.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use when adding a person with optional Org affiliations. For multi-entity free text, use add-lead.
- add-editorial-carousel: Generate a branded LinkedIn carousel (document post) for a piece from the BGA carousel skeleton. Composes N portrait 4:5 pages from the piece narrative (Why/How/What) using page-type primitives (cover, bullets, term, flow, compare, synth, cta - §5.8 catalogue), renders each page for a legibility gate, runs brand-review, delivers a swipeable PDF, wires it back into the piece `## Visuels`. Use when the user wants a carousel, a document post, or a live retex repurposed as swipeable pages.
- add-editorial-idea: Capture a new editorial idea (LinkedIn post, article, talk seed) as an anchor in `02-Areas/Éditorial/Ideas/`. Runs dedup check, applies frontmatter schema, enforces BGA brand conformity, updates MoC. Auto-detects express vs standard mode. Use when the user wants to capture, add, save, or register an editorial idea, post idea, article idea, or content seed.
- add-editorial-piece: Transform an editorial anchor (`Ideas/<file>.md`) into a piece for a given format (linkedin, article, live, podcast, talk). Resolves the anchor, fills frontmatter from template SSoT, drafts the body, runs brand conformity, ticks the matching line in the anchor's Déclinaisons checklist. Use when the user wants to draft a LinkedIn post, article, talk, live, or podcast piece from an existing idea.
- add-editorial-slides: Generate a branded HTML slide deck for a piece from the BGA slides skeleton. Composes slides from the piece narrative (Why/How/What, key points, tables) using slide-type primitives (title, bullets, cards, table, flow, callout, def, compare, probe, layers - §5.7 catalogue) selected per idea via the §5.7 archetype heuristic, renders each slide for a legibility gate, runs brand-review, wires the deck back into the piece. Interactive HTML opened in the browser, no delivery PNG. Use when the user wants intro slides, a live deck, or a talk/workshop deck for an editorial piece.
- add-editorial-visual: Generate a branded editorial visual (square post visual or LinkedIn event banner) for a piece from the BGA HTML skeleton. Reads the piece's `## Visuels` brief (format + disposition + setup/Why + contenu/How + synthèse/What), composes with CSS auto-layout (never hand-placed coordinates), renders HTML->PNG via Playwright, gates on visual legibility + brand-review, wires the asset back into the piece. Use when the user wants a schema, diagram, before/after, lifecycle visual, or event banner for a LinkedIn post, article, or live.
- add-formation: Bootstrap a new BGA formation by aggregating N editorial anchors (`Ideas/*.md`) into a curriculum. Creates the formation folder, generates the index from template, scaffolds one module file per anchor, backlinks each anchor via its Déclinaisons checklist, updates the Formations MoC. Supports direct mode (--ideas arg) or interactive mode (anchor picker grouped by pillar). Use when the user wants to create, scaffold, build, or initialize a training, workshop, masterclass, or curriculum.
- add-interaction: Create one CRM Interaction (dated exchange report) via add-interaction.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use to log a call/meeting/email/event tied to an Opp or Org.
- add-lead: Add a new prospect (Organisation + optional Opportunity + optional Contact) to the CRM. Accepts free text and/or LinkedIn URLs. Use when the user mentions a new company or contact to add.
- add-opportunity: Create one CRM Opportunity via add-opp.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use when adding a new channel/deal on an existing or new target Org. One Opp = one channel.
- add-organisation: Create one CRM Organisation via add-org.py (deterministic, schema-validated). Use when adding a single company (no opportunity/contact). For multi-entity free text + LinkedIn, use add-lead.
- archive-opportunity: Move a closed CRM Opportunity (perdu/gagne) to Opportunities/_archive/ via archive-opp.py (git mv, FK-safe). Use to declutter active pipeline after a deal closes.
- archive-project: Guided PARA archival of a finished project. Extracts forward-looking artefacts BEFORE the move - active backlog to Projects, living doc/SSoT to an existing or newly-created Area, structural decisions to ADRs, pure reference to Resources - sets the frozen marker, git mv to 04-Archives, propagates orphan wikilinks. Judgment-heavy (classify + route); writes = git mv + targeted edits. Use when a project is done and must be archived.
- brand-review: Audit a BGA editorial artifact (text and/or visual) against brand SSoT. Verifies tone-of-voice principles, format specs, color tokens, WCAG ratios, text/visual coherence. Outputs a status table + one prioritized recommendation.
- parse-td-results: Parse a Tutorial Dojo HTML exam result, extract incorrect questions, and append summaries to the AWS SAP Mistakes note.
- synthesize-interaction: Synthesize a freelance prospection Interaction draft - restructure the raw note and propagate to the linked Opportunity/Organisation. Thick orchestrator - LLM synthesis only, writes delegated to deterministic scripts.
- update-contact: Update an existing CRM Contact via update-contact.py (deterministic, schema-validated, idempotent). Set personal fields, append Org affiliations or notes.
- update-lead: Quick update of an existing Organisation or Opportunity from free text (informal conversation, phone call, ad-hoc info). Auto-detects the target. Use when the user reports info about an existing prospect.
- update-opportunity: Update an existing CRM Opportunity (non-status fields) via update-opp.py (deterministic, schema-validated, idempotent). For status/lost/won transitions use transition-opp.
- update-organisation: Update an existing CRM Organisation via update-org.py (deterministic, schema-validated, idempotent). Set durable company fields or append to body regions.
- weekly-actions: Display prospection actions for the current calendar week (Mon-Sun), including overdue items. Source - Opportunities. Use when the user asks for actions, planning, or prospection to-do.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

### Test privé (par surface)

Doctrine de pré-vol : valider la chaîne sans exposition publique ni notification réseau. Séquence du moins au plus réel : **1.** enregistrement local OBS (zéro diffusion) -> **2.** YouTube en *Private* (chaîne complète OBS -> Restream -> plateforme validée en privé) -> **3.** Twitch sur canal neuf (option). Le **profil LinkedIn perso reste éteint jusqu'au vrai lancement**.

| Surface | Test privé ? | Méthode |
|---|---|---|
| OBS (local) | Oui, zéro diffusion | Démarrer l'enregistrement / record-only Restream. Valide scènes, audio (Motu M2), cam, overlay chat |
| YouTube | Oui (vrai privé) | Destination Restream -> confidentialité **Private** (toi seul) ou **Unlisted** (lien only). Surface de référence pour valider la chaîne de bout en bout |
| Twitch | De facto | Canal BGA neuf (0 follower) = invisible + aucune notif ; ou laisser décoché dans Restream |
| LinkedIn page BGA | Oui | Créer un événement -> cocher **"This is a test event"** (visible admins + lien). Chat non supporté en mode test ; suppression immédiate si seul participant |
| LinkedIn profil perso | **Non** | Tout live y est public + notifie les followers -> tester via record-only ou YouTube-private, jamais un go-live de test |

22	
23	# Live - Terraform actions hors CRUD
24	
25	## Accroche
26	
27	Live technique, démos réelles dans le repo. Jeudi 30 juillet, 13h. LinkedIn + Twitch.
28	
29	Promesse : Terraform 1.14 fait entrer l'impératif dans le déclaratif. Le bloc `action` déclenche le day-2 (invalidation de cache, backup, job) depuis le lifecycle, en natif : visible au plan, exécuté par le provider. On le met à l'épreuve en direct sur deux démos AWS.
30	
31	## Corps
32	
33	### Conducteur - Terraform passe à l'action (live S31, jeu. 2026-07-30)
34	
35	Sujet direct (décision 2026-07-27, sans sondage - pool ADR-009 ouvert pour la suite). Démos = labs publics `examples/terraform-actions` (PR #27, CloudFront) et `examples/terraform-actions-lambda` (PR #28, Lambda/DynamoDB) sur [bgauduch/terraform-examples](https://github.com/bgauduch/terraform-examples). Découplage intact : le repo ne référence jamais ce live.
36	
37	Public : praticiens IaC et équipes plateforme qui portent du day-2 en scripts autour de Terraform. Héros : le **bloc `action`** (le mécanisme), pas les ressources des démos. Scène : terminal + navigateur (site CloudFront, console DynamoDB), micro-deck 3 slides max. Arc : **WHY (le day-2 vivait hors du plan) → WHAT teaser (action + action_trigger) → HOW x4 temps courts (action native A1·A2 · échappatoire Lambda B1·B2) → limites honnêtes → close**.
38	
39	Durée : live **≤ 1h, sans obligation de remplir**. Cœur ~38 min + Q&A généreuse.
40	
41	#### Idée-force du live : le day-2 rentre dans le plan
42	Jusqu'ici l'impératif post-provisioning (invalider un cache, sauvegarder avant mutation, lancer un job) vivait dans des `null_resource` + `local-exec` : hors plan, dépendant du CLI et des credentials ambiants, erreurs opaques. Le bloc `action` (v1.14, GA) le déclare : le *quoi* dans `action`, le *quand* dans `action_trigger` du lifecycle. La preuve au plan, l'exécution par le provider.
43	
44	**Le fil qui relie les deux démos** (choisi 2026-07-28, après répétition) : l'événement porte l'intention. `after_*` **publie une conséquence** du changement (l'invalidation suit la mise en ligne du nouveau contenu, T1) ; `before_*` **protège contre** le changement (le backup existe pendant que la table est encore dans son état d'avant, T2). Même mécanisme, deux familles d'événements, deux métiers du day-2. C'est l'arc qui transforme « deux démos AWS » en une seule histoire.
45	
46	#### Conducteur timé (~38 min cœur + Q&A, créneau ≤ 1h)
47	
48	##### 13h00-13h04 · WHY (S0, slide)
49	- Le constat : Terraform excelle au CRUD, le day-2 débordait en scripts hors plan. Cas vécus : invalidation CDN au déploiement, backup avant mutation.
50	- L'histoire du sujet : capacité présentée au vote de juin, restée sur le banc ; ses démos attendaient en PR, on les joue aujourd'hui.
51	- Versions posées d'entrée (fact-check) : `action` **v1.14, GA** ; events `before/after_create|update` uniquement ; destroy = v1.16 **alpha**, à venir - jamais « dispo ».
52	
53	##### 13h04-13h07 · WHAT teaser (S1, slide)
54	- Le couple : `action` déclare le *quoi* (config provider), `lifecycle.action_trigger` branche le *quand* (events). Schéma une ligne : événement → action → effet de bord prouvé.
55	- 4 actions AWS natives à date : `aws_lambda_invoke`, `aws_cloudfront_create_invalidation`, `aws_codebuild_start_build`, `aws_ec2_stop_instance`.
56	
57	##### 13h07-13h13 · HOW-A1 l'action visible au plan (T1, lab PR #27)
58	- Visite du lab : bucket S3 privé (OAC) + distribution CloudFront + `index.html` ; lecture ligne à ligne du couple - `action "aws_cloudfront_create_invalidation"` (le *quoi*) et `lifecycle.action_trigger` events `[after_create, after_update]` (le *quand*). Cœur didactique du live.
59	- Infra pré-appliquée (pre-flight) : le site répond, « Content version: v1 ».
60	- **Le geste déclaratif** : passer `content/index.html` en v2 → `terraform plan` → l'action apparaît au plan, annoncée à côté du diff de l'objet. L'effet de bord devient review-able avant toute exécution.
61	- Le why face à `local-exec` : dans le plan, credentials du provider, erreurs lisibles, événements réels du lifecycle.
62	- Pourquoi `after_update` ici : l'objet doit être dans le bucket avant de purger le cache. L'événement dit l'intention - `after_*` publie une conséquence (idée-force). Transition : « Le plan annonce l'action ; on la déclenche. »
63	
64	##### 13h13-13h20 · HOW-A2 le geste v1→v2 : l'invalidation part, le site suit (T1, terminal + navigateur)
65	- `terraform apply` → l'objet passe en v2, l'invalidation part dans la foulée, le site sert v2 immédiatement (l'invalidation court-circuite l'attente TTL).
66	- **Timing mesuré (répétition 2026-07-28) : 37 s** entre l'apply et le retour de prompt, parce que l'action **attend la fin de la propagation** avant de rendre la main. Temps de narration prévu : lire à voix haute les lignes `Invalidation … created, waiting for completion` puis `InProgress` puis `completed successfully`. C'est précisément la preuve que l'action est un citoyen de première classe du lifecycle, pas un script détaché.
67	- Preuve au navigateur : refresh → « Content version: v2 ». Point-clé en clôture de démo : **la conséquence du changement est publiée par le lifecycle lui-même.**
68	
69	##### 13h20-13h25 · HOW-B1 pourquoi l'échappatoire Lambda (T2, lab PR #28)
70	- L'objection qu'on pose d'entrée : « 4 actions natives, c'est court. » La réponse du lab : `aws_lambda_invoke` exécute **tout ce qu'une Lambda sait faire** - l'échappatoire générique.
71	- Visite du lab : table DynamoDB + Lambda de backup on-demand horodaté, `action_trigger` events `[after_create, before_update]` (lab corrigé 2026-07-28 : c'était `after_update`, ce qui sauvegardait l'état *d'après*). Le miroir de l'idée-force : `before_*` **protège contre** le changement - le filet existe pendant que la table est encore dans son état d'avant.
72	- Subtilité d'architecte : le cycle de dépendance évité (IAM de la Lambda scopé sur un ARN construit, jamais sur la table). Aparté : une action native `aws_dynamodb_create_backup` existe ; la Lambda démontre le mécanisme générique - préférer le natif quand il couvre.
73	
74	##### 13h25-13h30 · HOW-B2 le geste `ttl` : le filet avant la mutation (T2, terminal)
75	- **Le geste** : décommenter le bloc `ttl` sur la table (activation du TTL = vraie mutation day-2) → apply. À l'écran, l'ordre fait toute la démonstration : `Action complete` **puis** `Modifying...`. Le filet est posé avant que la table bouge (before_update).
76	- **Timing mesuré : 10 s** au total (mutation 5 s). Choix délibéré d'une mutation rapide : ajouter un index secondaire prenait **8 min 42** de `Still modifying...` en répétition, intenable en direct.
77	- Preuve côté AWS : `aws dynamodb list-backups` montre le backup horodaté (l'output `list_backups_command` donne la commande prête à coller).
78	- Bonus fort (première coupe si retard, cf Tips) : `terraform apply -invoke=action.aws_lambda_invoke.backup` - l'action à la demande, zéro changement d'infra (vérifié en répétition).
79	
80	##### 13h30-13h35 · Limites honnêtes + horizon (S2, slide)
81	- Events create/update only : le cas « cleanup/snapshot avant destroy » attend les events destroy d'`action_trigger`, **v1.16 alpha** ([CHANGELOG](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)). À présenter « à venir », jamais dispo - dernière stable 1.15.x.
82	- Couverture provider naissante (4 actions AWS) ; l'échappatoire Lambda comble.
83	- Quand rester en CI/pipeline : orchestrations multi-systèmes, longues, avec approbations. L'action = effet de bord court, couplé au lifecycle d'UNE ressource.
84	
85	##### 13h35-13h38 · CLOSE (S2)
86	- **Récap explicite**, une phrase par temps : le *quoi* (`action`), le *quand* (`action_trigger`), la preuve (au plan en A1, à l'écran en A2/B2 : invalidation + backup). Le fil : `after_*` publie une conséquence, `before_*` protège contre le changement.

88

# Live - Terraform actions hors CRUD

## Accroche

Live technique, démos réelles dans le repo. Jeudi 30 juillet, 13h. LinkedIn + Twitch.

Promesse : Terraform 1.14 fait entrer l'impératif dans le déclaratif. Le bloc `action` déclenche le day-2 (invalidation de cache, backup, job) depuis le lifecycle, en natif : visible au plan, exécuté par le provider. On le met à l'épreuve en direct sur deux démos AWS.

## Corps

### Conducteur - Terraform passe à l'action (live S31, jeu. 2026-07-30)

Sujet direct (décision 2026-07-27, sans sondage - pool ADR-009 ouvert pour la suite). Démos = labs publics `examples/terraform-actions` (PR #27, CloudFront) et `examples/terraform-actions-lambda` (PR #28, Lambda/DynamoDB) sur [bgauduch/terraform-examples](https://github.com/bgauduch/terraform-examples). Découplage intact : le repo ne référence jamais ce live.

Public : praticiens IaC et équipes plateforme qui portent du day-2 en scripts autour de Terraform. Héros : le **bloc `action`** (le mécanisme), pas les ressources des démos. Scène : terminal + navigateur (site CloudFront, console DynamoDB), micro-deck 3 slides max. Arc : **WHY (le day-2 vivait hors du plan) → WHAT teaser (action + action_trigger) → HOW x4 temps courts (action native A1·A2 · échappatoire Lambda B1·B2) → limites honnêtes → close**.

Durée : live **≤ 1h, sans obligation de remplir**. Cœur ~38 min + Q&A généreuse.

#### Idée-force du live : le day-2 rentre dans le plan
Jusqu'ici l'impératif post-provisioning (invalider un cache, sauvegarder avant mutation, lancer un job) vivait dans des `null_resource` + `local-exec` : hors plan, dépendant du CLI et des credentials ambiants, erreurs opaques. Le bloc `action` (v1.14, GA) le déclare : le *quoi* dans `action`, le *quand* dans `action_trigger` du lifecycle. La preuve au plan, l'exécution par le provider.

**Le fil qui relie les deux démos** (choisi 2026-07-28, après répétition) : l'événement porte l'intention. `after_*` **publie une conséquence** du changement (l'invalidation suit la mise en ligne du nouveau contenu, T1) ; `before_*` **protège contre** le changement (le backup existe pendant que la table est encore dans son état d'avant, T2). Même mécanisme, deux familles d'événements, deux métiers du day-2. C'est l'arc qui transforme « deux démos AWS » en une seule histoire.

#### Conducteur timé (~38 min cœur + Q&A, créneau ≤ 1h)

##### 13h00-13h04 · WHY (S0, slide)
- Le constat : Terraform excelle au CRUD, le day-2 débordait en scripts hors plan. Cas vécus : invalidation CDN au déploiement, backup avant mutation.
- L'histoire du sujet : capacité présentée au vote de juin, restée sur le banc ; ses démos attendaient en PR, on les joue aujourd'hui.
- Versions posées d'entrée (fact-check) : `action` **v1.14, GA** ; events `before/after_create|update` uniquement ; destroy = v1.16 **alpha**, à venir - jamais « dispo ».

##### 13h04-13h07 · WHAT teaser (S1, slide)
- Le couple : `action` déclare le *quoi* (config provider), `lifecycle.action_trigger` branche le *quand* (events). Schéma une ligne : événement → action → effet de bord prouvé.
- 4 actions AWS natives à date : `aws_lambda_invoke`, `aws_cloudfront_create_invalidation`, `aws_codebuild_start_build`, `aws_ec2_stop_instance`.

##### 13h07-13h13 · HOW-A1 l'action visible au plan (T1, lab PR #27)
- Visite du lab : bucket S3 privé (OAC) + distribution CloudFront + `index.html` ; lecture ligne à ligne du couple - `action "aws_cloudfront_create_invalidation"` (le *quoi*) et `lifecycle.action_trigger` events `[after_create, after_update]` (le *quand*). Cœur didactique du live.
- Infra pré-appliquée (pre-flight) : le site répond, « Content version: v1 ».
- **Le geste déclaratif** : passer `content/index.html` en v2 → `terraform plan` → l'action apparaît au plan, annoncée à côté du diff de l'objet. L'effet de bord devient review-able avant toute exécution.
- Le why face à `local-exec` : dans le plan, credentials du provider, erreurs lisibles, événements réels du lifecycle.
- Pourquoi `after_update` ici : l'objet doit être dans le bucket avant de purger le cache. L'événement dit l'intention - `after_*` publie une conséquence (idée-force). Transition : « Le plan annonce l'action ; on la déclenche. »

##### 13h13-13h20 · HOW-A2 le geste v1→v2 : l'invalidation part, le site suit (T1, terminal + navigateur)
- `terraform apply` → l'objet passe en v2, l'invalidation part dans la foulée, le site sert v2 immédiatement (l'invalidation court-circuite l'attente TTL).
- **Timing mesuré (répétition 2026-07-28) : 37 s** entre l'apply et le retour de prompt, parce que l'action **attend la fin de la propagation** avant de rendre la main. Temps de narration prévu : lire à voix haute les lignes `Invalidation … created, waiting for completion` puis `InProgress` puis `completed successfully`. C'est précisément la preuve que l'action est un citoyen de première classe du lifecycle, pas un script détaché.
- Preuve au navigateur : refresh → « Content version: v2 ». Point-clé en clôture de démo : **la conséquence du changement est publiée par le lifecycle lui-même.**

##### 13h20-13h25 · HOW-B1 pourquoi l'échappatoire Lambda (T2, lab PR #28)
- L'objection qu'on pose d'entrée : « 4 actions natives, c'est court. » La réponse du lab : `aws_lambda_invoke` exécute **tout ce qu'une Lambda sait faire** - l'échappatoire générique.
- Visite du lab : table DynamoDB + Lambda de backup on-demand horodaté, `action_trigger` events `[after_create, before_update]` (lab corrigé 2026-07-28 : c'était `after_update`, ce qui sauvegardait l'état *d'après*). Le miroir de l'idée-force : `before_*` **protège contre** le changement - le filet existe pendant que la table est encore dans son état d'avant.
- Subtilité d'architecte : le cycle de dépendance évité (IAM de la Lambda scopé sur un ARN construit, jamais sur la table). Aparté : une action native `aws_dynamodb_create_backup` existe ; la Lambda démontre le mécanisme générique - préférer le natif quand il couvre.

##### 13h25-13h30 · HOW-B2 le geste `ttl` : le filet avant la mutation (T2, terminal)
- **Le geste** : décommenter le bloc `ttl` sur la table (activation du TTL = vraie mutation day-2) → apply. À l'écran, l'ordre fait toute la démonstration : `Action complete` **puis** `Modifying...`. Le filet est posé avant que la table bouge (before_update).
- **Timing mesuré : 10 s** au total (mutation 5 s). Choix délibéré d'une mutation rapide : ajouter un index secondaire prenait **8 min 42** de `Still modifying...` en répétition, intenable en direct.
- Preuve côté AWS : `aws dynamodb list-backups` montre le backup horodaté (l'output `list_backups_command` donne la commande prête à coller).
- Bonus fort (première coupe si retard, cf Tips) : `terraform apply -invoke=action.aws_lambda_invoke.backup` - l'action à la demande, zéro changement d'infra (vérifié en répétition).

##### 13h30-13h35 · Limites honnêtes + horizon (S2, slide)
- Events create/update only : le cas « cleanup/snapshot avant destroy » attend les events destroy d'`action_trigger`, **v1.16 alpha** ([CHANGELOG](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)). À présenter « à venir », jamais dispo - dernière stable 1.15.x.
- Couverture provider naissante (4 actions AWS) ; l'échappatoire Lambda comble.
- Quand rester en CI/pipeline : orchestrations multi-systèmes, longues, avec approbations. L'action = effet de bord court, couplé au lifecycle d'UNE ressource.

##### 13h35-13h38 · CLOSE (S2)
- **Récap explicite**, une phrase par temps : le *quoi* (`action`), le *quand* (`action_trigger`), la preuve (au plan en A1, à l'écran en A2/B2 : invalidation + backup). Le fil : `after_*` publie une conséquence, `before_*` protège contre le changement.
- Repo + PRs en commentaire, pool de sujets ouvert pour le prochain live. → Q&A.

##### 13h38-14h00 · Q&A
- Marge volontaire, créneau ≤ 1h sans obligation de remplir. Live-troubleshooting, cas d'usage de l'audience.
- Amorces : « quel day-2 vit encore en script chez vous ? », « qui a déjà fait un local-exec dont il a honte ? » (auto-dérision, on l'a tous fait).

#### Pre-flight (mer. 29/07 soir + jeu. avant 13h)

Conséquence : **tout apply de T2 échoue** (`dial tcp 0.0.0.0:443: connection refused` sur la création du log group), y compris un simple refresh. Whitelister l'endpoint CloudWatch Logs sur le routeur ou basculer en partage de connexion mobile. Contrôle en une ligne : `dig +short logs.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` doit rendre une IP publique. Contournement de secours si le DNS résiste : exporter `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_CLOUDWATCH_LOGS=https://logs.eu-west-1.api.aws` avant l'apply (validé en répétition).
- **Répétition complète faite le 2026-07-28** sur le profil `sandbox` (compte 819926065482, eu-west-1) : les deux labs appliqués depuis zéro, les deux gestes live joués, `-invoke` vérifié, gates `fmt`/`validate`/`tflint`/`trivy` au vert en local.
- **État laissé en place, prêt pour le live** : T1 distribution `E1SKADQJ88A7ML`, site https://d77tmxluhcuzw.cloudfront.net qui sert **v1** (donc le geste v1→v2 fonctionne tel quel) ; T2 table `demo-tf-actions-lambda` fraîche, premier backup listé, bloc `ttl` commenté (donc le geste « décommenter » fonctionne tel quel). À re-vérifier la veille, l'état sandbox pouvant être nettoyé entre-temps.
- **Où jouer les démos** : deux worktrees git dédiés, qui portent le `terraform.tfstate` de la répétition (backend local). `~/git/oss/terraform-examples-live-s31-cloudfront` (T1) et `~/git/oss/terraform-examples-live-s31-lambda` (T2). Jouer depuis ces répertoires, sinon Terraform ne voit pas l'infra déjà déployée et voudrait tout recréer. Nettoyage après live : `terraform destroy` dans chacun, puis `git worktree remove`.
- **Appliquer les 2 labs la veille** si l'état a bougé. Repères mesurés : distribution CloudFront **2 min 42** à créer (jamais en direct), table + Lambda **35 s**.

Le rouge `commitlint` qui traînait était un faux positif corrigé à la racine par la PR #38 (le lint tournait sur la plage de push, qui après rebase embarquait des commits de `main`). - Terminal police 18-20px, thème clair (retex live 1 : code trop petit, chat trop gros) ; fallbacks : screenshots plan/invalidation/backups si réseau capricieux.

#### Tips & format live
- **Terminal = star** : micro-deck 3 slides seulement (S0 titre + tension · S1 mécanisme · S2 état des lieux) ; tout le reste se joue au terminal + navigateur.
- **Récap explicite au CLOSE, S2 à l'écran** (retex live 1 : l'audience l'a demandé).
- **Narration** : dire le *why* avant chaque geste, révéler l'output (les lignes d'invalidation, le `Action complete` avant `Modifying...`), pause. Les 37 s d'attente CloudFront = temps de narration prévu.
- **Timeboxing** : coupes prioritaires si ça déborde - (1) le bonus `-invoke` (juste le nommer), (2) l'aparté architecte IAM + action native DynamoDB (une phrase), (3) compresser Limites (la table S2 reste à l'écran, garder « quand rester en CI »). Garder intacts : les deux gestes (A2, B2), le fil `after_*`/`before_*`, le récap.
- **Registre « on »** participatif (tone 2.10) : on visite le lab, on lit le plan, on déclenche l'action.

**Pros** : l'impératif entre dans le plan (visible, review-able) ; credentials provider (rien d'ambiant sur le runner) ; events réels du lifecycle ; `-invoke` pour l'à-la-demande.
**Cons** : GA récent, couverture provider mince ; events destroy absents (v1.16 alpha) ; pas un remplaçant de la CI pour les orchestrations longues ; **l'apply attend la fin de l'action** (37 s mesurées sur l'invalidation), donc une action longue rallonge d'autant chaque apply, y compris en CI.

# CLAUDE.md - Éditorial

Rules for `02-Areas/Éditorial/`. Covers all content brands (BGA + personal).

## Structure

```
Ideas/                       # anchor notes - permanent intellectual asset (type: idee-editoriale)
Pieces/                      # content per format (type: piece)
  Formations/<slug>/         # aggregate format (type: piece-formation)
    index.md
    NN-<module>.md           # module per anchor (type: module-formation)
  Formations/_MoC Formations.md  # index of formations (vs Ideas/_MoC Idées.md for anchors)
Live/                        # live channel doctrine (type: area-doctrine) - lifecycle, stack, diffusion matrix, runbooks
assets/                      # ALL per-piece rendered visuals (ADR-006). Naming <format>-<sujet>.{html,png}, formats in design-system §5.0
ADRs/                        # architecture decision records (MADR-lite, index 00-adr-index.md)
enums.yml                    # executable SSoT of enums (read by lint-editorial.py)
scripts/lint-editorial.py    # linter + auto-fix (template + enums driven)
scripts/transcribe-vod.sh    # live VOD -> filtered transcript (retex source of truth)
Dashboard.md
```

Frontmatter schemas SSoT: `99-Templates/Template - Idee {Editoriale,Express}.md`, `Template - Piece LinkedIn.md`, `Template - Piece.md` (article/live/talk générique), `Template - Piece Formation.md`, `Template - Module Formation.md`. Don't redeclare.

## Idea lifecycle

- **Brute**: bullet line in `Ideas/_MoC Idées.md` §`Idées brutes (#No-Fomo, Bro !)`. Flat, no pillar, no file.
- **Anchor**: file in `Ideas/` with frontmatter. Indexed in MoC under `pillar`. Promote when ≥1 of: angle, source, planned declination.
- **Piece**: file in `Pieces/` per format. Naming: `YYYY-MM-DD <Format> - <Topic>.md` (date = created). Mandatory `idea: "[[anchor]]"` backlink (singleton, 1:1).
- **Publication**: on go-live, set `status: published` + fill `published-date` AND `url` (post/live permalink). Ask the author for the `url` when absent - capture it whenever a published piece is touched, never leave it empty.
- **Piece-formation**: folder in `Pieces/Formations/<slug>/`. `index.md` aggregates N anchors via `ideas: [...]` array. Each module file = 1 anchor (relation 1:1 module → anchor).
- Brutes >30 lines → promotion/archive pass.

## Rules

- **Layer separation** (airtight): branding = design semantics (`../BGA Consulting/Brand/`); editorial structure = forms/sections/enums (`99-Templates/` + this file); content = pieces (`Pieces/`). Never carry one layer into another. E.g. the `## Visuels` brief form is editorial structure (templates); its semantics (disposition recipes, Why/How/What arc, naming) stay branding §5.4; templates delegate by pointer, never restate it.
- Anchor↔Piece: backlink via piece `idea: "[[anchor]]"` only (mandatory on every piece). Schema (target / audience enums) in template SSoT.
- Anchor↔Formation: backlink via formation index `ideas: [...]` array (N:1). Anchor's Déclinaisons checklist tracks the link via `[x] Formation - [[<formation-index>]]`.
- **Live channel** SSoT: [[Doctrine - cycle de vie d'un live]] (`Live/`) - lifecycle, stack, diffusion matrix, TYPE checklists, runbooks.
	- Per-live RUN = the live piece: pre-live cases in `## Notes production`, follow-up in `## Suivi post-live`.
	- Timing/copy rules stay here (§Channel tactics).
- Default capture = brute.
- Pillars SSoT: `../BGA Consulting/Brand/01-Brief.md` §16.
- Evergreen snippets: `../BGA Consulting/Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md`.
- Cross-idea sources: `03-Resources/` wiki-linked from anchors.
- `#to-editorialize` tag on any note → process to brute or anchor, remove tag.
- Déclinaisons block in anchor: edited via `<!-- skill:editorial:declinaisons:start -->` / `:end` HTML anchors only.

## Concision

Applies vault `Note authoring` (root CLAUDE.md §Conventions). Editorial specifics:

- Per-type density quotas live in template headers (SSoT).
- Active voice, short sentences.
- No meta-prose ("in this section we'll...", "it is worth noting...").
- An idea exists in one place; other sections link to it.
- Code blocks: minimal viable, no boilerplate, no explanatory comments when code self-documents.
- Quality signal: if >3 lines can be cut without info loss, it's too long.

## Tooling

Linter SSoT: `scripts/lint-editorial.py` (consolidated, template-aware). Mandatory gate for every write in this area, by skill or by hand.

- Post-write (single file): `python3 02-Areas/Éditorial/scripts/lint-editorial.py --file <path> --apply` then re-run without `--apply` to confirm clean exit.
- Bulk audit: `python3 02-Areas/Éditorial/scripts/lint-editorial.py [--type ideas|pieces] [--apply] [--strict]`.
- Skills that touch ideas / pieces / formations / modules MUST call `--file <path> --apply` before returning, and report residual report-only violations to the user.
- Manual edits: run the same single-file command before commit when frontmatter, tags, headings, anchors, or backlinks were touched.
- Template drift (key absent from `99-Templates/`) → STOP, amend template first, then re-lint.
- Enums externalized: `enums.yml` (executable SSoT, hand-parsed, zero-dep). Linter reads it at runtime. See Data model & couplages for sync rules.

Visual generation: skill `add-editorial-visual` produces a piece's branded visual from its `## Visuels` brief (`format` + intention; `disposition` for square). Format dispatch, skeletons (`skeletons/<format>.html`), dims, naming, output home: design-system §5.0 registry. Render HTML->PNG via `../BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/render-html.mjs`; brand-review gate. ADR-006: all per-piece renders in `assets/`, never in `Brand/`.

Slides generation: skill `add-editorial-slides` produces a piece's branded HTML deck (slide-types per design-system §5.7, skeleton `skeletons/slides.html`), composed from the piece narrative. Legibility gate per slide (`?slide=N` via `render-html.mjs`) + brand-review; output `assets/slides-<sujet>.html` (interactive HTML, delivered as-is, no PNG). Wired into the piece `## Notes production` (live-support artifact), not `## Visuels`.

Carousel generation: LinkedIn document post (design-system §5.8, ADR-007), skeleton `../BGA Consulting/Brand/skeletons/carousel.html`. N pages portrait 4:5, composed from a piece (typically a live retex). Legibility gate per page (`?page=N`) + brand-review; **delivery PDF** via `_pipeline/render-pdf.mjs`; output `assets/carousel-<sujet>.{html,pdf}` (per-page PNG transient, not persisted). `carousel` is in the `visual-format` enum (it IS a `linkedin` piece's `## Visuels`, unlike slides). Generated by skill `add-editorial-carousel` (skeleton + per-page legibility gate + brand-review + PDF delivery + wire into `## Visuels` + lint), same filière as `add-editorial-slides`/`add-editorial-visual`; hand-craft from the skeleton stays possible.

## Data model & coupling

Home of the editorial data model (no separate `Modèle de données.md` - CRM lesson ADR-019). Structuring decisions: `ADRs/` (MADR-lite, index `ADRs/00-adr-index.md`); project context: sub-project `Gouvernance données éditoriales`.

Entities: `idee-editoriale` (anchor) · `piece` (per format) · `piece-formation` (index) · `module-formation` · asset (file in `assets/`).
Relations: anchor 1→N piece (FK `piece.idea`) · anchor N→1 formation (`formation.ideas[]`) · module 1:1 anchor (`module.idea`) · piece →N asset (body wikilink; `assets[]` frontmatter deferred) · piece →N lead→CRM (cross-area).

Coupling (who owns what, who reads, sync mode):

| Artifact                                                                                                                                   | SSoT of                                                                                                            | Read by                                                                | Sync                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `99-Templates/Template - *.md`                                                                                                             | frontmatter keys, headings, defaults                                                                               | `lint-editorial.py` (runtime)                                          | **auto** - the linter reads the template at runtime; changing a key CANNOT desync the linter                             |
| `enums.yml`                                                                                                                                | enum values (pillar/brand/format/status/target/audience) + legacy-tags + canonical-formats                         | `lint-editorial.py` (runtime)                                          | **auto** on the linter side                                                                                              |
| `enums.yml` ↔ human SSoTs: `../BGA Consulting/Brand/01-Brief.md §16` (pillar/target), root CLAUDE.md (format→template), templates (status) | business values                                                                                                    | human                                                                  | **MANUAL** - propagate on both sides, same commit                                                                        |
| `../BGA Consulting/Brand/03-Design-system.md §5.0` (registry) + §5.4/5.6 (specs)                                                           | `## Visuels` brief semantics, visual-format registry (format→dims/§/skeleton/naming/home), per-format design specs | templates (pointer), `add-editorial-visual`, `brand-review`            | **MANUAL** doc-to-doc                                                                                                    |
| asset naming `<format>-<subject>.{html,png}` (registry §5.0, ADR-006)                                                                      | §5.0                                                                                                               | `lint-editorial.py` (`ASSET_REF_RE`, extension-based, prefix-agnostic) | **MANUAL** - changing the extension → update §5.0 + linter regex; the format prefix is convention-only (no regex impact) |

Enums: values **in English**, **centralized in `enums.yml`** (ADR-005, keys + values). Templates and skills **point** to `enums.yml`, never restate values (so no template/skill ↔ enums drift). `visual-format` (square/event-banner) in `enums.yml`, format specs in design-system §5.0 registry; `disposition` (visual enum) points to §5.4. Reference to `enums.yml` = backticked path, never wikilink (non-note file).

Anti-drift rule: before touching a template, an enum, or asset naming, read the Sync column. **auto** coupling (keys/headings/enums read at runtime) cannot drift by construction. **MANUAL** coupling must be propagated in the same commit. The classic "template changes a field, linter out of date" = **auto** for keys (impossible); the real risk is enum value ↔ human doc and asset naming ↔ regex.

## Brand

- `brand: bga` - apply `../BGA Consulting/Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md` (positive phrasing, anti-positions, brand adjectives).
- `brand: personal` - free tone.
- **Copy corpus**: author-corrected copy keeps both versions in the piece.
	- `linkedin` → `## Version publication` · `live` → `🔬 Copy` block in `## Notes production`.
	- Typed delta logged in `../BGA Consulting/Brand/Corpus copy - généré vs validé.md` (3 occurrences → voice rule).

## Channel tactics

Channel-specific publication rules. Volatile (platform algorithms) - date each rule, revise on signal. `format` frontmatter = channel SSoT; pieces stay flat in `Pieces/` (folder only for inherently multi-file artifacts, e.g. `Pieces/Formations/`). Promote a channel to `Channels/<name>.md` only if its ruleset outgrows ~10 lines.

### LinkedIn

- Hashtags (rev. 2026-05-29): 3-5 max (>5 = reach penalty), 1 broad + niche, PascalCase, bottom of post, aligned to copy keywords. Marginal effect (passive SEO), not a reach lever. Tailor per topic, don't reuse one set. Re-validate if distribution shifts. Source: cross-research Sprout Social / ContentIn / ConnectSafely.
- Body: hook line 1 ≤220c (fold), standalone, no rhetorical-question opener (brand §4.1). External links → first comment, never in body. Code/identifiers as plain indented text (LinkedIn strips monospace).
- CTA discret (brand §4.1); omit for pure-technical posts.
- Visual: `square` format (SSoT design-system §5.0 registry + §5.4 spec, tokens + WCAG §1). Generated by skill `add-editorial-visual` (skeleton + brand-review gate), not by hand.
- Cadence: 1 post / 2 semaines (cf `Dashboard.md`).
- **Timing** (rev. 2026-07-07, priors best-practice B2B FR tech - **à recalibrer sur les analytics des posts**) : jours **mar/mer/jeu** (mardi + jeudi les plus forts en B2B ; lundi = bruit, ven après-midi + week-end = creux). Créneaux par ordre de reach : **matin 07h45-09h00** (prime, viser ~08h00), **déjeuner 12h-13h** (secondaire), **soir 17h30-19h** (tertiaire, mode détente). Poster **~15 min avant le pic** (golden hour : l'algo pondère l'engagement des 60-90 premières min). **1er commentaire (liens) posté dans la foulée** ; répondre aux premiers commentaires dans l'heure. **1 post / jour max** par profil (évite l'auto-cannibalisation). Programmation via le scheduler LinkedIn natif. Créneau retenu tracé à la programmation : pièce `live` → `## Notes production` ; pièce `linkedin` (pas de `## Notes production` au template) → tracking du projet/cadence porteur.
- **Rythme de promo d'un live** : annonce à runway (J-2/J-1, ou soir J-3 pour maximiser le save-the-date) + **relance jour-J ~08h** + **nudge ~12h50** (« on est live ») ; le live occupe le créneau déj. Un retex (carrousel) est evergreen → peut viser un prime slot standalone même décalé.
- **Promo d'un event/live (mécanique LinkedIn, rev. 2026-07-07)** : pour l'annonce, privilégier le **partage de l'event** (copy courte au-dessus) à un post texte + lien. La carte event est **cliquable → inscription directe + rappels auto**, et **native** (pas de pénalité « lien externe ») ; garder le 1er commentaire pour les liens externes (Calendly/repo). Le live génère un **post auto au démarrage** (copy générique, instant T) → l'annonce sert l'anticipation/l'inscription, un autre moment du funnel, donc pas redondante.

### Sondage choix de sujet (live)

Sondage LinkedIn faisant voter le sujet du prochain live. Règle (SSoT ADR-009) :
- Chaque option = item de backlog **ancré avant publication** (anchor `Ideas/` si riche, sinon brute dans `_MoC Idées.md`) ; le corps **wikilinke** chaque option vers son foyer.
- Pièce `format: linkedin` **taggée `sondage`**, filée comme tout post (via `add-editorial-piece`, gate linter).
- `idea:` (FK 1:1) pointe l'anchor **gagnant** ; multi-sujets → autres options cross-linkées dans le corps ; sondage ouvert → `idea:` provisoire, repointé sur le gagnant à la clôture.
- À la clôture : gagnant → `piece` `live` ; **options non retenues restent ancrées** (anchor `[ ] Live` ouvert, ou brute annotée `(sondage S<N>, non retenu)`) = pool réutilisable. Visibilité : Dashboard `## Sondages`.

.github/workflows/commitlint.yml

  +# Scoped to `pull_request`, not `push`: on a push the action lints the `before..after`
  +# range, which after a rebase or force-push spans commits already merged into `main`
  +# (release-please bodies carry a >100-char bot trailer) and fails a PR whose own commits

  +- **Lint commits on `pull_request`, never on `push`** - `wagoid/commitlint-github-action` lints `before..after` on a push event. C'est précisément la preuve que l'action est un citoyen de première classe du lifecycle, pas un script détaché.
- Preuve au navigateur : refresh → « Content version: v2 ». Point-clé en clôture de démo : **la conséquence du changement est publiée par le lifecycle lui-même.**
-##### 13h20-13h25 · HOW-B1 pourquoi l'échappatoire Lambda (T2, lab PR #28)
+##### 13h20-13h25 · HOW-B1 pourquoi l'échappatoire Lambda (T2, lab `examples/terraform-actions-lambda`)
- L'objection qu'on pose d'entrée : « 4 actions natives, c'est court. » La réponse du lab : `aws_lambda_invoke` exécute **tout ce qu'une Lambda sait faire** - l'échappatoire générique.

- Visite du lab : table DynamoDB + Lambda de backup on-demand horodaté, `action_trigger` events `[after_create, before_update]` (lab corrigé 2026-07-28 : c'était `after_update`, ce qui sauvegardait l'état *d'après*). Le miroir de l'idée-force : `before_*` **protège contre** le changement - le filet existe pendant que la table est encore dans son état d'avant.

- Subtilité d'architecte : le cycle de dépendance évité (IAM de la Lambda scopé sur un ARN construit, jamais sur la table). Aparté : une action native `aws_dynamodb_create_backup` existe ; la Lambda démontre le mécanisme générique - préférer le natif quand il couvre.

Merge fait, consolidation locale faite, pièce et projet à jour. Il reste la vérification AWS, qui demande ton login.

**Ce qui est en place**

| Étape | État |
|---|---|
| PR #27 CloudFront → `main` | ✅ `db4efcc` (squash) |
| PR #38 fix commitlint → `main` | ✅ `371fb5e` (débloquait la CI de #28, tu l'as validée) |
| PR #28 Lambda/DynamoDB → `main` | ✅ `c943cf4` (rebase + résolution du conflit README, CI verte 15/15) |
| Les 2 labs dans `~/git/oss/terraform-examples` sur `main` | ✅ contenu identique aux branches (diff vide) |
| `terraform.tfstate` des 2 démos migrés depuis les worktrees | ✅ copiés + `terraform init` OK en 1.14.9 |
| Pièce live : refs PR → chemins sur `main` | ✅ 6 endroits (conducteur, pre-flight, CTA, sources, 1er commentaire), lint 0 |
| Projet Outillage : tâche fix commitlint | ✅ cochée |

**Ce qui reste, et qui te demande une action**

1. **Login SSO** (token expiré) pour que je valide les states migrés :
```
! aws sso login --profile sandbox
```
Ensuite je lance `terraform plan` sur les deux labs. Attendu : *No changes* sur T1 et T2. **Tant que ce plan n'est pas vert, je ne supprime pas les worktrees** (ils portent la copie d'origine des states). La pièce décrit déjà l'état cible.

2. **DNS toujours bloquant** : `logs.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` → `0.0.0.0`. Le plan T2 échouera tant que ce n'est pas traité (whitelist routeur, ou `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_CLOUDWATCH_LOGS=https://logs.eu-west-1.api.aws`).

**Un point à trancher** : `examples/terraform-actions/content/index.html` porte le commentaire `Bump this version during the live demo, re-apply, and watch the after_update action invalidate...`. C'est un pointeur vers le live dans du code d'exemple, contraire au découplage repo↔live que le conducteur revendique. Reformulation neutre possible en un commit (`Bump this version, re-apply, and the after_update action invalidates the CloudFront cache automatically.`) : je le fais ?

terraform apply -invoke=action.aws_cloudfront_create_invalidation.invalidate

terraform destroy

# terraform-actions

> **Type**: `lab`
> **Tags**: `aws` `actions` `lifecycle` `cloudfront` `v1.14`

Terraform **1.14** introduced **actions**: declarative, *imperative* side-effects you bind to a
resource's lifecycle. This lab shows a classic day-2 need - **invalidate a CloudFront cache
automatically whenever the page it serves changes** - using the **native**
`aws_cloudfront_create_invalidation` action, with no `null_resource` + `local-exec` hack.

## The idea

Two new language pieces work together:

1. An **`action` block** declares *what* to do (here: invalidate a distribution).
2. An **`action_trigger`** inside a resource's `lifecycle` declares *when* to run it.

```hcl
action "aws_cloudfront_create_invalidation" "invalidate" {
  config {
    distribution_id = aws_cloudfront_distribution.site.id
    paths           = ["/*"]
  }
}

resource "aws_s3_object" "index" {
  # ... uploads content/index.html ...
  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.aws_cloudfront_create_invalidation.invalidate]
    }
  }
}
```

Available lifecycle events: `before_create`, `after_create`, `before_update`, `after_update`.

The event encodes the intent. Here the invalidation **publishes a consequence** of the change, so it
runs `after_update` - the new object must be in the bucket before the cache is purged. The companion
`terraform-actions-lambda` lab takes the mirror case: a backup that **protects against** the change,
on `before_update`.

## Why not `local-exec`?

A `null_resource` + `local-exec "aws cloudfront create-invalidation ..."` works, but: it is not in

# AGENTS.md - terraform-actions example

Guidance for AI coding agents working inside this example. Repo-wide conventions live in the root
`AGENTS.md`; this file covers what is specific to `terraform-actions`.

Taxonomy: **type `lab`** - progressive, playable in a live session. Tags: `aws`, `actions`,
`lifecycle`, `cloudfront`, `v1.14`.

## Purpose and scope

A **pedagogical demo** (supporting content for a live tech session, 30-45 min). It illustrates
Terraform 1.14 **actions**: binding the native `aws_cloudfront_create_invalidation` action to an
S3 object's lifecycle so the CDN cache is invalidated on every content change.

Keep it minimal and focused on the action mechanism. Do not add production hardening (WAF, access
logging, custom ACM domain) unless asked - those are documented as out-of-scope in the README and
silenced with `#trivy:ignore` lines.

## Architecture

Single root module (this directory; `providers.tf` is auto-discovered by CI). Flow:

`random_id` → `aws_s3_bucket` (private, OAC-only) → `aws_cloudfront_distribution` →
`action "aws_cloudfront_create_invalidation"` → `aws_s3_object.index` whose `lifecycle.action_trigger`
runs the action on `after_create` / `after_update`.

The action references the distribution; the object's trigger references the action. Terraform
orders the action after the distribution exists - do not add explicit `depends_on` for this.

## Common commands

```bash
terraform init
terraform apply                 # after_create -> first invalidation
# edit content/index.html, then:
terraform apply                 # after_update -> new invalidation
terraform apply -invoke=action.aws_cloudfront_create_invalidation.invalidate   # stand-alone
terraform destroy
```

Validation before committing: `terraform fmt -recursive` (root) and `terraform validate` here.

## Prerequisites

- Terraform `>= 1.14.0` (pinned to `1.14.9` in `mise.toml`).
- AWS provider `6.41.0` (carries the CloudFront invalidation action).
- AWS credentials for `apply`; default region `eu-west-1`.

## Conventions in this example

- Prefer the **native provider action** over Lambda/local-exec; the Lambda escape-hatch variant
  lives in `terraform-actions-lambda`.
- `events` are bare identifiers (`after_create`, not `"after_create"`).
- Bucket stays private (OAC + bucket policy scoped to the distribution ARN); never make it public.
- Tags via `local.common_tags` (`Project` / `ManagedBy`); follow the same shape for new resources.

Cost Explorer, compte sandbox `819926065482` (profil `billing-ro`, coût réel, pas une estimation) :

| Jour | Total compte |
|---|---|
| 26/07 | 0,0001 USD |
| 27/07 | 0,0001 USD |

| 29/07 | 0,0000 USD |
| **Juillet à date** | **0,11 USD** |

C'est cohérent avec ce qui est déployé, aucune ressource des deux labs n'a de coût à l'heure :

- **CloudFront** : pas de facturation à l'heure, uniquement requêtes + transfert (quelques refresh). Invalidations : 1000 chemins/mois gratuits.
- **DynamoDB** : `PAY_PER_REQUEST`, donc zéro capacité provisionnée. PITR + backup on-demand facturés au Go-mois sur une table quasi vide.
- **Lambda** : au repos, gratuit. **CloudWatch Logs** : rétention 14 j, quelques Ko.
- **S3** : le bucket + `index.html`, d'où les 0,0002 USD du 28.

Deux réserves : Cost Explorer a ~24 h de latence (le 29/07 est partiel), et les chiffres sont au niveau du compte, donc ils couvrent aussi les restes des autres labs. Rien n'accumule.

`git log --all -- '*.tfstate'` vide, aucun blob `tfstate`/`.terraform/` dans le graphe d'objets, non suivis aujourd'hui, ignorés par `.gitignore:8`. # AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, Aider, etc.) working in this repository. A `CLAUDE.md` symlink points here so Claude Code picks it up automatically. Each example also has its own nested `AGENTS.md` with example-specific guidance - read it before editing inside an example.

## What this repo is

A **library of self-contained Terraform examples**. Each lives under `examples/<name>/` and is independent: its own `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, tooling (`mise.toml`, `.tflint.hcl`) and Terraform root module(s). Examples are **not** factored into shared code - isolation is intentional so each can be read, run, and live-demoed on its own.

Use cases served: reusable patterns, illustrations for blog/LinkedIn posts, and starting points / labs for live tech sessions.

## Taxonomy

Every example declares a primary `type` plus free-form tags. Source of truth is the catalogue table in the root `README.md`; each example's `README.md`/`AGENTS.md` restates its type.

- `pattern` - reusable, production-leaning reference.
- `lab` - starting point / TP with progressive steps for a live session.
- `experiment` - preview/RC features, may be intentionally unstable.

Do **not** create top-level category directories (`patterns/`, `experiments/`...). Keep `examples/` flat and classify via `type` + tags. This avoids lifecycle churn when an example changes category.

## How to add an example (golden path)

1. `mkdir examples/<name>/` - kebab-case, scope-first (`aws-multi-env`, `terraform-rc-variables`).
2. Add `README.md` (state its `type` + tags, objective, run steps) and `AGENTS.md` (example-specific guidance).
3. Add per-example tooling: `mise.toml` (pins `terraform`, may be an RC/prerelease for `experiment` types; inherits `tflint`/`trivy` from the repo-root `mise.toml`) and `.tflint.hcl`.
4. Add the Terraform root module(s). Any directory containing a `providers.tf` is auto-discovered by CI - no CI edit needed to validate it.
5. Register a row in the root `README.md` catalogue table.

## CI

`.github/workflows/terraform.yml` auto-discovers Terraform root modules (directories containing `providers.tf`) under `examples/` and runs `validate` + `tflint` + `trivy` per module in a matrix. `terraform fmt -check -recursive` runs once at the root. The `tf-setup` composite action installs the toolchain via `jdx/mise-action` from the target module's merged `mise.toml` (terraform, tflint, trivy). Adding an example requires no CI change.

## Toolchain (mise)

[mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) is the **single source of truth (SSOT)** for every CLI tool, locally and in CI - there is no separate version file or per-tool CI setup step.

- **Root `mise.toml`** pins repo-wide tools (`tflint`, `trivy`) plus a default `terraform`. **Per-example `mise.toml`** overrides only `terraform` (versions legitimately differ per example) and inherits the rest, since mise merges every `mise.toml` from the cwd up to the repo root.
- **Add a new tool once, in `mise.toml`** (root if repo-wide, example if local). Never re-pin a tool as a CI input - CI installs whatever `mise.toml` declares.
- **Renovate** bumps these via its native `mise` manager; alpha/beta/rc pins (e.g. `experiment` examples) are frozen by a `packageRule` matching `currentValue`.
- **Tasks replace Makefiles**: run with `mise run <task>`, list with `mise tasks`. Each task runs in a subshell, so a task's `cd` (or `dir`) never leaks into your interactive shell.
- **Locally**: `mise install` once, then tools resolve automatically per directory (use `mise exec -- <cmd>`, or activate mise in your shell).

## Repository standards

- **Language**: English everywhere in committed content - code, comments, identifiers, docs, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, script output strings. No other language, including inside an example. (This repo is read on screen and public; mixed languages stand out.)
- **Git flow**: GitHub flow (short-lived feature branches off `main`, PR review, squash-merge). Name branches `<type>/<kebab-summary>` where `<type>` is a Conventional Commit type (`feat`, `fix`, `build`, `ci`, `docs`, `chore`, `refactor`, `test`) - e.g. `build/mise-toolchain-ssot` - so branch names stay consistent with commit messages and PR titles.
- **Work tracking**: durable backlog = GitHub Issues + Milestone (a goal + its acceptance criteria); each PR references its issue (`Closes #N`). `main` carries no task file - session plans stay local/ephemeral. `tasks/lessons.md` holds durable repo lessons.
- **Commit messages**: [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) - `<type>(<scope>): <subject>`. Use the example name as scope when relevant (e.g. `feat(aws-multi-env): ...`).
  - Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `chore`, `refactor`, `test`, `ci`, `build`.
  - Breaking changes: append `!` after type/scope or add a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
  - Keep subject imperative, lowercase, no trailing period, ~72 chars max.
  - Enforced in CI: `commitlint.yml` (commit messages, config-conventional) and `pr-title.yml` (semantic PR title, since squash-merge uses the PR title).
- **Versioning**: [SemVer](https://semver.org/), repo-level single release line via release-please.
- **Validation before commit**: `terraform fmt -recursive` (root) and `terraform validate` inside each touched root module. Optional local mirror of the CI gates lives in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (fmt/validate/tflint + conventional commit-msg); enable with `pre-commit install --install-hooks && pre-commit install --hook-type commit-msg`.

=== em-dash (—) repo-wide ===
AUDIT-PROMPT.md:1:# Mission — Audit à blanc, diff, et système pérenne (run Fable 5)
AUDIT-PROMPT.md:12:Phase 0 physically archives the previous audit corpus into `audit/_archive/2026-07-opus-run/` **before any analysis**. Until R2 explicitly starts, **never read anything under `audit/_archive/`**. Allowed evidence: module code itself, **in-repo consumer code (`patterns/`, other modules' examples) — consumption patterns are in scope**, `audit/reports/.scans/` (raw scanner JSON), `audit/reports/.metrics/` (metrics pack), `audit/reports/.oss/*.json` (OSS probe records), git history of `modules/`. This blindness is the point: an anchored counter-expertise is worthless.
AUDIT-PROMPT.md:14:## Locked decisions (inputs — do not re-litigate)
AUDIT-PROMPT.md:16:1. **OSS consumption strategy = vendor + override** as group default (no private Terraform registry at the client, small team). Mandatory guardrails: active upstream drift detection (scheduled job comparing the vendored pin to latest upstream tag), `vendor/` technically locked (CODEOWNERS + CI check, all changes through the sync process), pattern reserved for leaf/shallow modules, **license gate** (upstream license verified compatible with in-repo vendoring — Apache-2.0/MPL-2.0 OK, copyleft/BUSL = blocker; attribution/NOTICE file kept in `vendor/`), **transitive-dependency policy** (upstream module consuming other modules: inject-first — disable the embedded feature and inject the resource as input, e.g. `create_kms_key=false` + key ARN — else scripted transitive vendoring: resolve the tree via `.terraform/modules/modules.json`, rewrite sources, license gate cascades; note inject-first neutralizes runtime creation but NOT the init-time source fetch while the module block exists). Proxy registry = documented target evolution (the internal Artifactory registry distributes the product catalog; what is missing is an OSS proxy remote).
AUDIT-PROMPT.md:20:## Decision grid — 4 questions, 4 verdicts
AUDIT-PROMPT.md:24:- **Q0 — Raison d'être** : ce besoin mérite-t-il un module du catalogue ? (Un wrapper passthrough de 1-3 ressources sans logique ni garde-fous = un pattern documenté suffit peut-être.)
AUDIT-PROMPT.md:25:- **Q1 — OSS** : un module OSS de référence sain couvre-t-il le besoin ?
AUDIT-PROMPT.md:26:- **Q2 — Wrapper** : le delta interne s'exprime-t-il en wrapper mince au-dessus de cet OSS ? Mince = ≈ < 50 lignes de **logique** (tags, défauts, validations, petite orchestration) ; le pur passthrough de variables/outputs re-déclarées est **exclu du compte**.
AUDIT-PROMPT.md:27:- **Q3 — Viabilité** : le code interne est-il assez sain et bien conçu pour valoir son coût de correction et de run ?
AUDIT-PROMPT.md:29:Verdict ∈ {`KEEP` (garder, mettre à l'état de l'art), `WRAP-OSS` (remplacer par vendor+override de l'OSS), `REBUILD` (réécrire, OSS absent/mort), `RETIRE` (supprimer le module, documenter un pattern à la place)}. Q0 non → RETIRE. Q1+Q2 oui → WRAP-OSS, **sauf si l'item 10 (trajectoire de possession) ou l'item 2 (immunité cascade-diff déjà payée en interne face à un upstream dense en data sources) penche nettement KEEP — dans ce cas KEEP avec justification explicite chiffrée (coût de migration + sync burden vs coût de run interne)**. content.content: # UpdateTimeToLive The `UpdateTimeToLive` method enables or disables Time to Live (TTL) for the specified table. A successful `UpdateTimeToLive` call returns the current `TimeToLiveSpecification`. It can take up to one hour for the change to fully process. Any additional `UpdateTimeToLive` calls for the same table during this one hour duration result in a `ValidationException`. TTL compares the current time in epoch time format to the time stored in the TTL attribute of an item. If the epoch time value stored in the attribute is less than the current time, the item is marked as expired and subsequently deleted. **Note** The epoch time format is the number of seconds elapsed since 12:00:00 AM January 1, 1970 UTC. DynamoDB deletes expired items on a best-effort basis to ensure availability of throughput for other data operations. **Important** DynamoDB typically deletes expired items within two days of expiration. The exact duration within which an item gets deleted after expiration is specific to the nature of the workload. Items that have expired and not been deleted will still show up in reads, queries, and scans. As items are deleted, they are removed from any local secondary index and global secondary index immediately in the same eventually consistent way as a standard delete operation. For more information, see [Time To Live](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/TTL.html) in the Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide. ## Request Syntax ``` { "TableName": "{{string}}", "TimeToLiveSpecification": { "AttributeName": "{{string}}", "Enabled": {{boolean}} } } ``` ## Request Parameters The request accepts the following data in JSON format. **Note** In the following list, the required parameters are described first. ** [TableName](#API_UpdateTimeToLive_RequestSyntax) ** The name of the table to be configured. You can also provide the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the table in this parameter. Type: String Length Constraints: Minimum length of 1. Maximum length of 1024. Required: Yes ** [TimeToLiveSpecification](#API_UpdateTimeToLive_RequestSyntax) ** Represents the settings used to enable or disable Time to Live for the specified table. Type: [TimeToLiveSpecification](API_TimeToLiveSpecification.md) object Required: Yes ## Response Syntax ``` { "TimeToLiveSpecification": { "AttributeName": "string", "Enabled": boolean } } ``` ## Response Elements If the action is successful, the service sends back an HTTP 200 response. The following data is returned in JSON format by the service. ** [TimeToLiveSpecification](#API_UpdateTimeToLive_ResponseSyntax) ** Represents the output of an `UpdateTimeToLive` operation. Type: [TimeToLiveSpecification](API_TimeToLiveSpecification.md) object ## Errors For information about the errors that are common to all actions, see [Common Error Types](CommonErrors.md). ** InternalServerError ** An error occurred on the server side. ** message ** The server encountered an internal error trying to fulfill the request. HTTP Status Code: 500 ** LimitExceededException ** There is no limit to the number of daily on-demand backups that can be taken. For most purposes, up to 500 simultaneous table operations are allowed per account. These operations include `CreateTable`, `UpdateTable`, `DeleteTable`,`UpdateTimeToLive`, `RestoreTableFromBackup`, and `RestoreTableToPointInTime`. When you are creating a table with one or more secondary indexes, you can have up to 250 such requests running at a time. However, if the table or index specifications are complex, then DynamoDB might temporarily reduce the number of concurrent operations. When importing into DynamoDB, up to 50 simultaneous import table operations are allowed per account. There is a soft account quota of 2,500 tables. GetRecords was called with a value of more than 1000 for the limit request parameter. More than 2 processes are reading from the same streams shard at the same time. Exceeding this limit may result in request throttling. ** message ** Too many operations for a given subscriber. HTTP Status Code: 400 ** ResourceInUseException ** The operation conflicts with the resource's availability. For example: + You attempted to recreate an existing table. + You tried to delete a table currently in the `CREATING` state. + You tried to update a resource that was already being updated. When appropriate, wait for the ongoing update to complete and attempt the request again. ** message ** The resource which is being attempted to be changed is in use. HTTP Status Code: 400 ** ResourceNotFoundException ** The operation tried to access a nonexistent table or index. The resource might not be specified correctly, or its status might not be `ACTIVE`. ** message ** The resource which is being requested does not exist. 1	# terraform-actions-lambda
2	
3	> **Type**: `lab`
4	> **Tags**: `aws` `actions` `lambda` `dynamodb` `v1.14`
5	
6	Terraform **1.14** actions can run **provider-native** side-effects (see `terraform-actions` for a
7	CloudFront invalidation). But the provider only ships a handful of native actions. This lab shows
8	the **escape hatch**: `action "aws_lambda_invoke"` lets a lifecycle event run **any logic you can
9	put in a Lambda**. The illustration: take a **timestamped on-demand DynamoDB backup** before
10	Terraform ever mutates the table.
11	
12	## The idea
13	
14	```hcl
15	action "aws_lambda_invoke" "backup" {
16	  config {
17	    function_name   = aws_lambda_function.backup.function_name
18	    payload         = jsonencode({ table_name = local.table_name })
19	    invocation_type = "RequestResponse"
20	  }
21	}
22	
23	resource "aws_dynamodb_table" "this" {
24	  # ...
25	  lifecycle {
26	    action_trigger {
27	      events  = [after_create, before_update]
28	      actions = [action.aws_lambda_invoke.backup]
29	    }
30	  }
31	}
32	```
33	
34	The Lambda (`lambda/backup.py`) just calls `dynamodb.create_backup(...)` - but it could do
35	*anything*: call a third-party API, post to Slack, run a data migration. That is the point.
36	
37	## Why `before_update` and not `after_update`
38	
39	The event you pick encodes the intent. `after_*` publishes a consequence of the change (the
40	companion `terraform-actions` lab invalidates a CDN cache *after* new content is uploaded).
41	`before_update` protects against the change: the snapshot is taken while the table is still in its
42	previous state, so an unwanted schema or capacity change is recoverable. In the apply output the
43	action completes **before** `Modifying...` on the table.
44	
45	`after_create` still fires once, on creation - there is nothing to back up before a table exists.
46	
47	> A native `aws_dynamodb_create_backup` action actually exists. We deliberately go through Lambda
48	> here to demonstrate the generic mechanism - reach for a native action first when one fits.
49	
50	## Avoiding the dependency cycle
51	
52	The table's `after_create` action invokes the Lambda, so the Lambda must **not** depend on the
53	table (that would be `table → action → lambda → table`). The Lambda's IAM policy therefore scopes
54	`dynamodb:CreateBackup` to an ARN built from `var.region` + the caller account id + the table name
55	(`local.table_arn`), not from `aws_dynamodb_table.this.arn`.
56	
57	## What gets deployed
58	
59	- A DynamoDB table (`PAY_PER_REQUEST`, point-in-time recovery + SSE enabled).
60	- A Python Lambda + least-privilege IAM role (`dynamodb:CreateBackup` on the table, write to its own
61	  log group) and an explicit CloudWatch log group with retention.
62	
63	## Prerequisites
64	
65	- **Terraform `>= 1.14.0`** (pinned to `1.14.9` via `mise.toml`; actions do not exist before 1.14).
66	- **AWS provider `6.41.0`** (carries the `aws_lambda_invoke` action).
67	- AWS credentials for `apply` (`validate`/`plan` need none). Default region: `eu-west-1`.
68	
69	## Run (live demo)
70	
71	```bash
72	terraform init
73	terraform apply        # creates the table + Lambda; after_create fires the FIRST backup.
74	
75	# See the backup the action just created:
76	aws dynamodb list-backups --table-name "$(terraform output -raw table_name)" --region eu-west-1
77	```
78	
79	Then, the day-2 change:
80	
81	```bash
82	# Uncomment the `ttl` block on aws_dynamodb_table.this in main.tf, then:
83	terraform apply        # before_update fires a NEW timestamped backup, then the table is modified.
84	```
85	
86	Pick a **fast** mutation to demo this: enabling TTL or changing tags settles in ~5 s, while adding a
87	global secondary index takes several minutes of `Still modifying...`.
88	
89	Invoke the action **stand-alone** (back up on demand, no infra change):
90	
91	```bash
92	terraform apply -invoke=action.aws_lambda_invoke.backup
93	```
94	
95	Teardown:
96	
97	```bash
98	terraform destroy      # on-demand backups survive table deletion - remove them manually if needed.
99	```
100	
101	## Going further
102	
103	- `terraform-actions` - the same mechanism with a **native** provider action (CloudFront), and the
104	  `after_update` counterpart of the event choice discussed above.
105	
106	## Troubleshooting
107	
108	- `dial tcp 0.0.0.0:443: connect: connection refused` on `logs.<region>.amazonaws.com` - a local
109	  DNS filter (Pi-hole, AdGuard, router-level ad blocking) is blackholing hostnames starting with
110	  `logs.`. Allow-list the CloudWatch Logs endpoint; the AWS SDK does not fall back to the
111	  `logs.<region>.api.aws` dual-stack name on its own.
